pr_title: Fix `do_server()` socket from remaining open after `naccept` is supposed to reach `0`
pr_body:
When `-naccept` is passed to `s_server`, the listening socket remains open while handling clients, even after `naccept` is supposed to reach `0`.

This is caused to to the decrementation of `naccept` and closing of the socket happening a little too late in the `do_server` function.

This causes a weird behaviour where clients can still connect to the server, but will never be handled (instead of just getting rejected by the OS).

Fixes https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/26229.

issue_context.title: Server socket remains open when using `naccept` in `s_server` (Fix available)
issue_context.body:
When using `s_server` with `naccept`, the listening remains open even after accepting `n` clients.

This is caused by the decrementation and check of `naccept` being too late in the `do_server` function in `s_socket.c`.

I have opened a PR to fix this issue: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/26228

Thanks!

review_comments: Doesn't this break things for DTLS (i.e. where `type != SOCK_STREAM`)?

Additionally, I'm not sure I see what the problem is here.  naccept from the man page indicates that it only allows the server to accept <naccept> connections before exiting.  The fact that the listener remains open doesn't imply that that the server will call SSL_accept on the listening socket again, so I'm not sure what the issue is here

The server does not call SSL_accept, but since it is configured to listen with a backlog, it essentially accepts clients on the TCP level.

Moreover, when using `openssl s_server` as a utility, it cannot be run sequentially where each process only handles one client, as it keeps the socket open.

@mattcaswell This won't break it as this logic is already inside a `type == SOCK_STREAM` check.

It might not decrement naccept, but I will submit another change to address that.
I have updated my commit to include a change that addresses `type != SOCK_STREAM` cases.
